Elena / Tessa — attaching the initial CSV exports and a short note on methodology. Summary here: 

Methodology (short):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated pool, A100s (4x), model: open-llm-16k-v2 (quantized), sequence lengths representative of your workload (prompt ~120 tokens, gen up to 256).
- TTFT definition: end-to-end measured at client SDK from request send to first token received. We capture median, p95, p99 and provide raw per-request timestamps in perf_results_v1.csv.
- Throughput/concurrency: ramp tests at concurrency steps [1,4,8,16,32,64,128] for 10-minute windows; steady-state computed over final 5 minutes.
- Repeatability: each step run 3x, we include mean and std in CSV.

Key highlights (preview):
- Median TTFT at concurrency=1: 78ms (median), p95 210ms, p99 360ms
- At concurrency=64 steady-state QPS ~ 48 req/s, median TTFT increased to 180ms (p95 410ms)
- TTFT variability tied to KV cache miss windows; we note cache warmup behavior in the CSV and slides.

Attachments: perf_results_v1.csv, ttft_latency_summary.csv (full per-step exports). I'll also flag any runs that had transient errors.

If you want, Karthik and I can include a short note mapping these numbers to cost-per-1M tokens estimates for your target concurrency.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Perf Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference

Elena — confirmed. We've uploaded the deliverables to the shared Drive folder and pinned links below. Contents of the package (final):

- perf_slide_exec_summary_v1.pdf — 1-page exec + 3 method/result slides (10-min readout)
- perf_results_v1.csv — full per-request export (timestamped rows)
- ttft_latency_summary.csv — aggregated med/p95/p99 by concurrency step
- map_timelines.xlsx — MAP milestones & PO close dates (for your procurement team)
- system_topology.png — simplified diagram showing request path and cache layer
- Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/overview/acme-HUB-4792 (live charts + export buttons)
- Recording: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_map_perf_bundle (walkthrough recording and slides)

Notes on cache warmup (slide notes):
- Warmup pattern: first 30–90s show higher TTFT variance as KV caches populate. For steady operating points we recommend a short pre-warm (50 concurrent synthetic warm requests) during traffic shifts.
- Recommended operating point: concurrency 16–32 for best latency/cost balance for your current workloads (see slide 2).

We will run one last short verification test on June 2 AM PT and upload any small revisions. Otherwise, we are on track for the June 3 readout and to have artifacts available to your procurement team for June 7 PO issuance.

Thanks — looking forward to the readout.

Tessa Morgan
